exposure: economic support from multiple earning members
cohort: A total of 502 postpartum mothers from five hospitals in Kumasi, Ghana were included in the study.
finding: Education attainment, economic support, planned pregnancies, physical exercise, and exclusive breastfeeding were protective factors against postpartum depression, while being a single mother, cesarean sections, and spontaneous vaginal deliveries increased the risk.
mod_finding: Both cesarean sections and spontaneous vaginal deliveries were found to increase the risk of postpartum depression.
